bib.title: Chapter 14: Psychology (Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.)

question: How do reinforcement learning prediction, control, credit assignment and model-based/model-free ideas correspond to what psychologists found about animal learning?
contributions: Presents the Rescorla-Wagner model and its real-time generalisation, the TD model of classical conditioning
Maps eligibility traces and TD value functions onto stimulus traces and conditioned reinforcement for delayed reward
Maps model-based/model-free RL onto cognitive maps and goal-directed/habitual control
Clarifies terminology differences between RL and psychology (reward vs reinforcement signal, control, action)

results.claim: Rescorla-Wagner update is an error-correction rule driven by prediction error (surprise), equal to the LMS/Widrow-Hoff rule; it explains blocking.
results.setup: Trial-level model, linear features x(s) of CS presence, aggregate strength v(s,w)=w.x(s); delta_t = R_t - v(S_t,w_t)

results.claim: The TD model replaces the trial-level update with a real-time TD(lambda) update using TD error and eligibility traces; with gamma = 0 it reduces to Rescorla-Wagner.
results.setup: Linear function approximation, backward view of semi-gradient TD(lambda); delta_t = R_{t+1} + gamma v(S_{t+1}) - v(S_t)

results.claim: The TD error contains the term gamma v(S_{t+1}) - v(S_t), which is why TD learning yields second-order and higher-order conditioning; a temporal difference counts like a US.
results.quote: implying that as far as learning is concerned there is no di↵erence

results.claim: In the simulated second-order conditioning run, first-phase training brings CSB's associative strength to 1.65.
results.setup: TD model, presence representation, phase 1: CSB trained with US; phase 2: CSA paired with CSB without US
results.quote: to predict a US so that its associative strength increases, here to 1.65.
results.note: CSA's strength rises then falls as CSB extinguishes.

results.claim: Hull hypothesised stimulus traces decay to zero after 30 to 40 seconds, giving the goal gradient; longer gradients came from conditioned reinforcement passing backward.
results.setup: Hull's theory of delayed reinforcement in instrumental conditioning

results.claim: Thorndike's cats cut puzzle-box escape time with experience.
results.setup: Cats in puzzle boxes, successive experiences

results.claim: RL has two mechanisms for credit assignment under delayed reward, eligibility traces and TD-learned value functions, matching stimulus traces and secondary reinforcement.
results.setup: Actor-critic: TD error from critic is conditioned reinforcement to the actor
results.quote: providing an immediate evaluation of performance even when the primary reward signal

results.claim: Shaping (reinforcing successive approximations) is a powerful tool when rewards are sparse.
results.setup: Skinner's pigeon bowling example; starting with easier problem and increasing difficulty
results.quote: powerful technique for computational reinforcement learning systems as well.

results.claim: Model-based agents adapt to a changed reward through planning without new experience; in the Fig 14.5 maze a goal reward changing from 4 to 1 switches the best return to 3.
results.setup: Hypothetical two-step maze, goal rewards 4,0,2,3; reward right of S2 changed 4 to 1

results.claim: Latent learning: animals learn environment models without reward, analogous to model-based RL.
results.quote: environment models can be learned even without explicit rewards or penalties.

limits: Chapter says RL as described is not intended to model animal behaviour details; TD model is neither complete nor perfect and needs model-based elements and adaptive parameters.

Qualitative accounts of classic experiments; no new data, and few quantities (1.65, 25 steps, alpha/lambda/gamma) come from simulations adapted from Sutton and Barto 1990 / Ludvig et al. 2012; effect sizes and sample sizes of animal experiments are not given.
Presence and CSC representations are admitted to be unrealistic neural hypotheses.
Authors concede modelling of reinforcement schedules and behavioural vigor is not well developed; single scalar reward ignores separate appetitive/aversive systems.
Omits psychology of decision making, ethology, and multi-agent RL.
Written 2018; no mention of LLM-era RL.
practices: Use shaping (start with an easier problem, raise difficulty) when rewards are too sparse for any non-zero signal (p.360).
Provide a critic's TD error as immediate conditioned reinforcement to an actor when primary reward is delayed (p.363).
Restrict the action set A(s) / use instinct-like priors to make learning easier (p.359).
Explore in some form; any guided exploration works provided exploration exists (p.359).
Combine model-free and model-based control; trust the one with higher confidence (p.368).
Keep reward signal and reinforcement signal distinct: reinforcement = reward plus value difference (p.374-375).

terms.definition: Occurs when an animal fails to learn a CR when a potential CS is presented along with another CS that had been used previously to condition the animal to produce that CR.
Occurs when a previously-conditioned CS acts as a US in conditioning another initially neutral stimulus.
A stimulus that consistently predicts primary reinforcement and becomes a reinforcer itself.
Trial-level error-correction model: an animal only learns when events violate its expectations; equivalent to the LMS rule.
Real-time model with TD error, eligibility traces and discounting over stimulus representations.
How do you distribute credit for success among the many decisions that may have been involved in producing it? (Minsky 1961)
Training an animal by reinforcing successive approximations of the desired behavior.
In modern terms, an environment model or model of an animal's task space; learned without reward and used for planning.
Habits are triggered by stimuli and performed automatically (model-free); goal-directed behavior is controlled by knowledge of goal values and action consequences (model-based).
After rewarded learning the reward value of an outcome is changed, to zero or negative; tests habitual vs goal-directed control.
A number that multiplies a vector to determine parameter updates in a learning algorithm; includes TD error.
